clue.text: After church, longed to take a tea inside? Took certain steps

indicators.note: After church means the church abbreviation stands first, with the rest following it
longed to take something means the word for longed holds the next pieces
inside confirms that the tea pieces sit within the word for longed

parts.note: ached means yearned or longed
cha is an old slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Someone back from church yearns for a cup of tea indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' and 'inside' together put the tea pieces within the longing word. 'Took certain steps' is a past-tense verb, like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To cha-cha-cha is to dance the Latin ballroom dance, whose footwork is a set pattern of steps.

clue.text: Reversal of shares in spec had failed, leaving one short

indicators.note: shares in spec means the share word goes inside the jumbled letters
had failed tells us the letters of spec and had come out wrong, so rearrange them
Reversal of says the synonym for shares is read backwards

parts.note: parts means shares or portions

explanation.surface: A financial speculation collapses after shares turn back, leaving an investor out of pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had failed' rearranges SPECHAD into letters that sit around the reversed shares word. 'leaving one' just joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short means lacking money, which is exactly the state of someone with no spare funds.

clue.text: Therapy can transform this druggie with art

indicators.note: can transform says the letters of therapy can be reworked into this word together with art

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Art therapy might rehabilitate an addict.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of THERAPY rearrange to the answer plus ART, so take ART out of THERAPY and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is Chambers' slang for a drug addict, short for hypodermic.

clue.text: Leader of choir, one to separate its extreme members

definitions.text: Leader of choir, one to separate its extreme members

indicators.note: to separate the end letters something has to go between them
the extreme members are the first and last letters of the word choir

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choirmaster's job is to keep apart the outliers at either end of the stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extreme members' picks the outer letters of 'choir', which the two short words split. The whole clue also describes the person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantor is the precentor who leads singing in a church or synagogue choir.

clue.text: Confirmed boozer? His heart drops only a bit as doubles appear

indicators.text: His heart drops only a bit
indicators.note: the middle letter of the drinker's word slips down just one place in the down entry

parts.note: an alkie is a slang word for an alcoholic

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker's heart is barely affected, though he starts seeing double.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of ALKIE is K; moving it one place lower in the down light gives ALIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubles look identical, so 'as doubles appear' means the same in looks.

clue.text: Criminal in a nick? Its contents are few

indicators.note: criminal tells us the letters of in a nick are put together in a crooked way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A villain locked up in a police cell suggests a crook in the nick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for a police station or prison, but here its letters are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A canikin is a small can or drinking vessel, so it holds little.

clue.text: Element of this synonym describing 'difficult' fit

indicators.note: Element of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A thesaurus note says this synonym applies to a tantrum thrown by a difficult person.
explanation.definitionFit: A hissy fit is a tantrum, so hissy is the adjective used for that kind of difficult outburst.

clue.text: Policemen abroad, one facing a risk when rumbled?

indicators.note: facing means standing in front of, so the one letter goes before the rest

parts.note: a means one, as the indefinite article

indicators.note: rumbled suggests something disturbed and shaken up, so the letters of a risk are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Foreign police officers face danger when they are found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when rumbled' turns A RISK into SKARI; askari is a Swahili-derived word, often used as its own plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Askari were native soldiers or police in East Africa, a foreign force to a British solver.

clue.text: Unruly youth had up with older female, one behind bars?

indicators.note: had up in a down light means the youth's word is turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth known for rowdiness
aînée is the French for elder, feminine, used in English for an older sister

explanation.surface: A tearaway is brought before the court along with an older woman and locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had up' makes DET from TED. 'Had up' also hints at being taken to court, which misleads. A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A detainee is a person held in custody, such as a prisoner in a cell.

clue.text: Cures onset of twinge in bust? It's common among bathers

indicators.note: in tells us the curing word and the twinge's first letter go inside the word for bust

parts.note: broke means bust, having no money
reast is a Scots and dialect verb meaning to cure bacon by drying or smoking

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Some remedy is sought for a sudden twinge in the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like the chest, but it means penniless. Reast is a rare Scots verb, so the curing word is the hard part.
explanation.definitionFit: The breaststroke is a swimming style seen everywhere among swimmers.

clue.text: Seat missing head and leg making sort of slide?

indicators.note: missing head means the word for seat loses its first letter

parts.note: a chair is a seat
pins is slang for legs, so a pin is a leg

explanation.surface: A chair without its top and a leg would end up sliding over.
explanation.walkthrough: A hair slide is the British term for a barrette, the clip worn in hair. 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin is a clip for holding hair in place, a kind of hair slide.

clue.text: Sloppy work is accepted by roofing specialist

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken inside it

parts.note: a slater lays slates on roofs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slapdash job is waved through by the roofer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaister is a Scots word for a messy mess or slovenly task, so it means careless work.

clue.text: Backing raps, go at a lick

indicators.note: backing means the word for raps is read from the back

parts.note: to knap is to strike or rap smartly

explanation.surface: Getting a telling-off, someone is told to hurry along.
explanation.definitionFit: To spank along means to move quickly, the same as travelling at speed.

clue.text: Time in Scottish isle for a local spree

indicators.note: time in the isle means the time letter goes inside the island name

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Time spent on a Hebridean island is a chance for a binge with the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' marks the word as dialect, here Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyte is a Scots word for a drinking bout or wild outing.

clue.text: Neck ornament from outfit that is reversed in greeting

indicators.note: in places the turned pieces within the greeting word

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting

indicators.note: reversed applies to both the outfit word and the abbreviation, read backwards together

parts.note: kit means an outfit of gear
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An ornament worn round the neck from someone's outfit is turned round during a welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns KITIE into EITIK, which goes between H and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A hei-tiki is a Maori greenstone pendant carved as a human figure and worn round the neck.

clue.text: An Asian has relocated in this ancient ME city (5, apostrophe)

indicators.note: has relocated says the letters of an Asian are moved round, leaving the word in beside the answer

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Asian has moved house to an old Middle Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: AN ASIAN rearranges to the answer plus IN. ME is Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Sana'a is the capital of Yemen, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities.

clue.text: Transformed bore's snorting cocaine, in the grove

indicators.note: snorting means taking in, so the drug letter goes inside the jumbled word
transformed says the letters of the bore's are rearranged

parts.note: C is a slang abbreviation for cocaine

explanation.surface: A tedious man changed after taking cocaine in a woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: BORES rearranged by 'Transformed' gives SROBE, which takes in C. The clue as held reads 'grove' where the dictionary sense is groove.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrobe is a furrow, as in the channel on an insect's snout for its antenna.

clue.text: In which every early Irish lord ruled here

indicators.note: In says the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An early Irish chief governed in a place where everyone was ruled.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the C of 'which' and ends at the E of 'early'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheverye is a Spenserian form of chiefery, an Irish chieftaincy or the chief's lands.

clue.text: Caged creatures often having distorted leg and ribs

indicators.note: distorted means the letters of leg and ribs are bent into a new shape

explanation.surface: Caged pets often have a misshapen leg and ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerbils are small rodents commonly kept as pets in cages.

clue.text: Cheers when right gets in — outstanding

indicators.note: the right word gets in, inserted into the toast

parts.note: prosit is a toast, like cheers
a lien is a legal right over property

explanation.surface: People call out a toast when their candidate wins a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' looks like the political right, but it is a legal claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosilient is a rare word meaning prominent, standing out.

clue.text: Old verse form isn't reproduced in the main

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters within the sea word

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the sea

indicators.note: reproduced means made again, with letters arranged differently

explanation.surface: An old poetic form isn't reprinted in the principal editions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduced' rearranges ISNT into STIN. 'The main' is the open sea in old poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestina is a poem of six six-line stanzas with repeated line-end words, an old verse form.

clue.text: Enchantress bewitched mariner entering dingy hovel?

indicators.note: entering links the hut word and the jumbled sailor so one sits inside the other
bewitched says the letters of mariner are put under a spell and jumbled

parts.note: a ken is slang for a house, often a disreputable one

explanation.surface: A sorceress casts a spell on a sailor who walks into a grubby hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bewitched' rearranges MARINER into REIMNAR, and 'entering' must be read as taking the hut word inside, not going into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reimkennar is Scott's word for a sorceress who works spells through rhymes.

clue.text: Flat bracket as once seen in a funnel?

indicators.note: seen in places the old word for as inside the hybrid animal's name

parts.note: a funnel is a hybrid of a horse and a donkey, which Chambers lets the word mule loosely cover
ut is an obsolete word for as, from the Latin

explanation.surface: An old-style flat support visible inside a ship's chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funnel' looks like a ship's chimney or a cone, but here it is the rare name for a horse-donkey hybrid, and the question mark admits the loose match.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutule is the flat projecting block under a Doric cornice, a kind of bracket.

clue.text: Wild and woolly creature, girl in a state

indicators.note: girl in a state means the girl word goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl gets into a frenzy about a woolly animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild and woolly' looks like a description of the girl's state, but it defines a wild sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The argali is a large wild sheep of Asia with a thick coat.

clue.text: Wretched characters in drain, rock bottom

indicators.note: wretched suggests the letters of drain are in a bad state, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Miserable people in a gutter have hit the lowest point.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything.

clue.text: Injure the hooves of old brutes made to work

indicators.note: made to work suggests the letters of brutes are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: Old beasts of burden forced to labour have sore feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' marks the word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: To surbate or surbet was to make the feet sore through walking, especially an animal's.

clue.text: Not properly burnt, unchanged with a bit of lotion applied

parts.note: same means unchanged

indicators.note: a bit of the lotion is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sunburn left as it is, with a dab of cream applied.

clue.text: Hide on front of ancient shield

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Skin stretched over the face of an old shield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, conceal, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelta was a small light shield in ancient Greece.

clue.text: North African location that's fresher according to taste

explanation.surface: A North African city tastes fresher.

clue.text: Very little in press turned up? Not good

parts.note: Chambers gives lie as meaning to press, to weigh on
V is the abbreviation for very, a little piece of the word

explanation.definitionFit: Evil means wicked, the opposite of virtuous.

clue.text: Poke round centre of pus in swelling

indicators.note: the centre of a three-letter word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A doctor prods around a pus-filled lump.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud flesh is swollen tissue, and proud means raised above a surface.

clue.text: Fusillade from religious campaigner

explanation.surface: A burst of gunfire from a preaching activist.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of fire from many guns; Salvo is Australian slang for a Salvation Army member.

clue.text: Something like a porthole on side of cruise vessel, cosmetic

parts.note: an eye is a small round opening, much as a porthole is
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A round window on the side of a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on side of' joins the two pieces. 'Cosmetic' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun, make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is make-up drawn around the eyes.

clue.text: Republican in Dail melee's involved here? (11, two words)

parts.note: taken as written
